Reform the Ninjago: Legends page by LB07productions

Reform the Ninjago: Legends page by LB07productions[]

It seems clear that there hasn't been a clear vision on how the Ninjago: Legends page and the new shorts should be treated as. While the page was originally intended as a subtheme similar to Legacy and Core, the term Ninjago: Legends has now become more than just a subtheme, with new shorts being branded under this name (Tales from the Monastery of Spinjitzu and The Virtues of Spinjitzu were branded and treated as part of the main show). So a quick recap on how corresponding pages were structured on the wiki:

Before Kai's Monstrous Journey was announced:

  • The Ninjago: Legends page was treated the same way as the other subthemes.
  • Ninjago Legends: Monstrosity was treated as a titled series of shorts (Similar to how Star Wars animation would have multi-season shows like The Clone Wars and limited series of shorts like Tales of the Jedi). Italicized and written under "sub-heading 1" as it wasn't branded under Dragons Rising.

After Kai's Monstrous Journey was announced, I had decided to have the shorts be a part of the Monstrosity series (through the use of clunky citations) as the Legends page was considered a subtheme page, and writing these shorts as a titled series called Kai's Monstrous Journey wouldn't be that correct since it still uses the Legends logo.

So, the suggestion I make is to change the Legends page, and treat that as the series that would house Monstrosity, Monstrous Journey and future projects. So for example, the page could start as: "Ninjago: Legends is an anthology Ninjago series comprised of short mini-series. It began with Monstrosity in June of 2025."

If this would happen, I would also suggest that Ninjago Legends: Monstrosity would be renamed simply to Monstrosity, similar to Ninjago seasons not being titled "Ninjago: Prime Empire" for example (the page's first line would be structured similarly to Decoded). And in this press release featuring crew members found by Litemods, they all simply call it "Monstrosity." This would also apply to future named Legends installments.

Change how the Legends page is operated

Support

  1. LB07productions 14:53, August 29 2025 (UTC)
  2. I agree with everything. Matt600 (talk) 19:03, 29 August 2025 (UTC)

  5. Brandini N (talk) 01:21, 30 August 2025 (UTC)

(Use Glen Lakin's Source Week element explanations as article quotes) by Brandini N

(Use Glen Lakin's Source Week element explanations as article quotes) by Brandini N[]

This isn't exactly an "important" proposal, but I think this would be a neat change. During this Source Week, Glen Lakin has given us his reasonings and explanations as to why certain elements fall under certain Sources - poetic ones at that. As such, I think that most of his saying could be used as the main quotes on element articles. We're already doing this with every Source's pages already; plus, these quotes provide more insight to the elements in question, especially a lot of the ones introduced in DR Season 2. Of course, some people like myself may have certain preferences with some elements quote, moreso with the ones from The Book of Elemental Powers, but overall, adding these new quotes would give these elements some fresh modernity in tandem with the concept of the Source Dragons. Create a page for Corrupted Ones by Legor4ik

It's now time to address an elephant in the room. An elephant that is only younger than the franchise itself only by two years. We don't have a page for people corrupted by Dark Matter! (recreate the "Ninjago: Legends" sets subthem page in addition to the current page ) by PixX26

(recreate the "Ninjago: Legends" sets subthem page in addition to the current page ) by PixX26[]

Following LB07productions vote, the page Ninjago: Legends became a serie page instead of a set subtheme page in order to list all installments branded under "Ninjago: Legends" and this was a good things in my opinion. But I don't think this page should exist at the to the detriment of existence of the original subtheme page. It is a thing to have a page to house all Legends series but it is another to make the sets subtheme page disappear. Ninjago: Legends is above all a Ninjago sets subtheme like Ninjago: Legacy and Ninjago: Core were. They are all 3 subthemes that coexist with the main theme (which is now subtitled "Dragons Rising"). Since there is no real series called "Ninjago : Legendes", when wiki viewers search for "Legends" in most cases they are looking for the sets subtheme. I therefore propose to have two pages entitled "Ninjago: Legends", one for the sets one for the medias. This is an unprecedented case because Ninjago: Legend is an unprecedented case as specified by LB07 in his proposal, Ninjago: Legends designates a Lego subtheme but is also the name under which several media contents are branded which was not the case of Legacy of Core.

The current page would be renamed "Ninjago: Legends (series)" (or another name if you have something better to suggest) and the new page about the sets will simply be titled "Ninjago: Legends" because once again Legends is above all a subtheme of LEGO sets.

I am convinced that this is the solution to make things clearer and not neglect part of the concept of Ninjago: Legends.

Support

  1. PixX26 (talk) 12:11, 2 September 2025 (UTC)
  2. Samurai viper (talk) 03:18, 5 September 2025 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. As a mentioned before, the name of the theme is and has always simply just been Ninjago/NINJAGO, even now on LEGO.com, it's not called Ninjago: Dragons Rising, even in 2017-18 they had one page for the movie and the show. You do know that Masters of Spinjitzu and Dragons Rising are at their core, designed to be a toyline. Currently, Ninjago: Dragons Rising is the dominant line of sets, but we don't have a separate page for the product line. The Legends page beforehand was just isolating the same information from the sets page. The two sets were also moved to and listed in the Monstrosity page as the commercial for it features [albeit newly made] clips from Monstrosity. LB07productions (talk) 13:49, 2 September 2025 (UTC)
  2. The Ninjago sets page lists the movie as a subtheme as well, and we don't have a page for the movie sets subtheme, which ran simultaneosly with the show in 2018, just like "Dragons Rising" and "Legends", so why should Legends be treated differently, especially since currently, the sets-show relationship in Legends is just like the show, with even marketing campaigns and commercial having the sets and Monstrosity listed together as a unified work. Also regarding Legends not being recognized as a series, all descriptions of Monstrosity refer it as a series. ElementalPilot 04:55, September 5 2025 (UTC)
  3. Casting vote: Matt600 (talk) 12:40, 8 September 2025 (UTC)

Neutral

Comments

  1. Dragons Rising and Legends are far from being the same case. Dragons Rising is a show, Legends is not. Monstrosity and Kai's Monstrous Journey are. They are simply branded under the same title, which is why it was good to make a page that brings them all together, but that does not make Ninjago: Legends an officially recognized series. When people search for Dragons Rising on the wiki they search the show, when they search the Legends's series (in the plural), they search "Kai's Monstrous Journey" and "Monstrosity"/"Ninjago Legends: Monstrosity". (Status of Thunderfang and the Forbidden Five) by Matt600

(Status of Thunderfang and the Forbidden Five) by Matt600[]

I propose that Thunderfang and the Forbidden Five's status be changed from "Unknown" to "Deceased".

There has been a discourse about this and I discussed it with other staff members but we decided to make a vote for everyone. I think there is nothing that suggests TF or the FF are alive after the events of S3P2. That doesn't mean they cannot come back but there is no cliffhanger or anything to suggest it. Their souls/spirits vanquished and because they were technically already deceased (lacking physical bodies) it is safe to say they are deceased as of S3E20.

My edit was reverted due to comparisons with other characters like Iron Baron, the Omega, and Empress Beatrix. However, I think Thunderfang’s case is very different. Iron Baron was seen again in the magazines and made noises in the episode itself, which suggests he may have survived. The Omega simply disappeared off-screen, leaving his fate ambiguous. Beatrix was lost, not killed or anything. These characters all have room left for speculation — but Thunderfang’s defeat suggests no other possible outcome.

I also feel that if we avoid labeling characters as deceased just because they might come back someday, we’ll never be able to use the "Deceased" status at all. For example, Harumi seemed clearly dead, yet was later resurrected. That doesn’t mean she wasn’t dead in the meantime. Similarly, even if Thunderfang’s spirit could return somehow, his physical body was destroyed, which technically makes him deceased. Characters like Zarkar are also considered deceased until proven otherwise and this seems similar to me.

Thunderfang's final appearance clearly shows his destruction. Until we get contradictory evidence in future content, I believe "Deceased" is the most accurate status based on what we’ve seen on-screen. But that's only my opinion and I am open to discussion so feel free to argue.

Support

  1. Matt600 (talk) 20:52, 13 September 2025 (UTC)
  2. PixX26 (talk) 21:29, 13 September 2025 (UTC)
  3. Arthurwyne (talk) 01:06, 14 September 2025 (UTC)

Gender field in infobox 2.0 by Akita the Formling

Gender field in infobox 2.0 by Akita the Formling[]

Matt made a proposal about this four years ago, and I myself would like to bring this proposal back on the wiki. As we all know, we already have Gender on the Creature infobox, but we do not have it on the Character infobox. There are categories that tell us the genders of characters, but as Matt stated all these years ago, most people overlook or never go to those categories, or don't even know they exist, although they are indeed at the top. I don't know everything that happened back then, but putting the Gender in the Character infobox was dropped. Yes, a character's gender could also be obvious, but I think it would be unnecessary and/or inconsistent for one to have Gender in their infobox and the other one doesn't. Establish a way genders for characters are listed by LB07productions

Establish a way genders for characters are listed by LB07productions[]

Recently, many pages for talking animals specifically have had their genders changed to unknown because allegedly, their voice actors' genders are not a strong enough reason for their gender to be determined, as their pronouns need to be explicitely said.

While on first glance, I can the see the reason for not wanting to misgender characters, but the arguments used to ground these points are flawed once analysed. For example, the Strength Dragon has its gender unknown because characters younger male characters sometimes have female voice actors, or the only example for the opposite, Mystake used to have male voice actors to achieve her grumpy raspy voice. The former is a common thing that occurs in voice acting and shouldn't be used for a comparison with other characters. The second argument is that the wiki misgendered the Life Dragon which lacks a central context: I had made the Life Dragon page last year and had assumed that the voice actor was female the same way Motion was, but once it was discovered they were played by a non-binary actor, the gender was changed to unknown as they were the first non-binary character listed on the wiki. Thirdly, why would the show cast male actors to play non male characters if the series would go out of their way to cast a non-binary actor to play exclusively non-binary characters. And finally, we have already previously changed unknown pronoun characters' genders to match with their actors: Terri from the movie, so through that same logic, that should be the default for others unless something else is stated.

(Treat the homeworlds/homelands of the deceased/undead differently) by Brandini N

(Treat the homeworlds/homelands of the deceased/undead differently) by Brandini N[]

The homeworld/homeland field for character infoboxes is meant to list a character's realm (or region) of origin/birth (i.e. the First Spinjitzu Master was born in the First Realm, despite being known primarily as the guy from ninjago). Simple, right? However, there are a few complications that arise for those who are undead or deceased (or alive but ghost, if you catch my drift). For characters such as the Skulkin and Ghost Warriors, many individuals' homeworlds are listed as Ninjago, though in many such cases there is no evidence to support these claims, so technically in these situations the field should be left as "Unknown."

That being said, Skulkin and Ghost warriors also have their applicable afterlife realm categories on their pages. These categories are for "every inhabitant, creature, location, and object that can be found in this realm," and while they can be found in those realms, they are not their realms of origin. However, all deceased individuals that transition to an afterlife realm are treated as in a "new state of existence," so waking up in the Departed, Cursed, and Underworld realms would for all intents and purposes be a "second homeworld." This rule of thumb is applied for a majority of deceased characters, adding both the homeworld category and the afterlife realm, but I believe this should be applied to the infobox as well.

To summarize, a residents of the Underworld, Departed Realm, Cursed Realm (the latter two prior to the Spectral Lands fusion) should list both their original homeworlds (formerly) and their current afterlife realm. Additionally, in the cases of the Skulkin and Ghost Warriors, when applicable, the homeworlds should be listed as unknown. Specific cases where reasonings and deductions can be used, like Samukai and Soul Archer can used the current listed realms.

(Consider the Greenbone warriors magazine comics as non-canon) by PixX26

(Consider the Greenbone warriors magazine comics as non-canon) by PixX26[]

The comics of issue 23-27 and issue 30 of the Ninjago: Legacy Magazine should not be considered canon because they are inconsistent :


Presence of the Earth Dragon and the Ice Dragon who have never appeared in any other canon content prior Dragons Rising, and the Water Dragon (Core) that never appeared anywhere else. No explanation for their presence. While the ninjas having dragons companions always had an explanation : Guardian of the Golden Weapons then liberation from Imperium. Plus We have never considered the presence of the Earth and Ice dragon in these comics as canon as this is not even mentioned in their respective history sections that simply begin with Dragons Rising.

Presence of Steeper Wisdom, while it stopped working for a long time and it only appeared in non-canon content so far (Wu's tea short). knowing that ninja wear their Core suit that they are supposed to wear only between Season 15 and the Merge. Once again no justification for this appearance and why the ninjas would still have this tea shop (which again they never had in the canon story) while it is clear that tea seller is not part of their activity or that of master Wu during the Season 7 to The Merge period.

The fact that neither Kai nor the bone king seem to recognize each other when they meet in episode 13 Which means they have not met and fought before. Gulch's argument is really not a good one considering him not recognize Zane is turned in a humorous way and is something assumed unlike the case of Kai/Bone King.

The green bone warriors in these comics are never presented as inhabitants of the Underworld which is the case in the canon story. They just live in Ninjago in the comics. Moreover in issue 27 the bone king says that he missed the heat of the sun when he was locked underground which is not consistent with the fact that he comes from an underground realm where there is no sun.

Bonnus: the fact that the bone king and the greenobone leader wear helmets with one of the five Bone Weapons when they are supposed to be destroyed in the comics. Yes it could be replicas but once again it creates a gap between the comic and the show that need to be filled by speculative additions.

These comics have too many unexplained appearances that came out of nowhere for it to work with canon. These comics work as a standalone story detached from any other storyline exactly like the Core theme.

Considering these comics as non-canon would facilitate and simplify the story of the bone king and the greenbone warriors similarly to the story of Crab tooth, because we would not need to add speculative information such as

  • Crossed bones are replicas
  • Kai and the bone king miraculously forgot what they looked like
  • The ninjas had an ice dragon, an earth dragon and a water dragon only during this period ane they disappeared after that
  • The greenbone traveled to Ninjago by an unknown means
  • The ninja reportedly reopened a non/canon tea shop only during the period of this comics and it never reappeared elsewhere.

Change the Ghost Warriors' original homeland to Ninjago by LB07productions

Change the Ghost Warriors' original homeland to Ninjago by LB07productions[]

Recently, following the vote to implement addiotional homelands to deceased characters before the Merge. The Skulkin's original homeland was kept as Ninjago while all Ghost Warriors except for Morro and the Soul Archer have been changed to unknown. I think that that the Cursed Ghost Warriors seen in Possession should have their homeland changed back to Ninjago for the following reasons:

The show heavily implies that the Ghost Warriors used to live in Ninjago before their deaths. While other villanous factions like the Serpentine are shown to be chaotic in human civilization as shown in "The Royal Blacksmiths," the Ghost Warriors were shown to be relatively peaceful on their own, such as when the two warriors who were walking on a bridge before Ronin destroyed it in "Stiix and Stones" or after they imprisoned the Stiix citizens and were eating together in "Curseworld, Part I."

Another factor is the designs, as seen with Morro and the Anacondrai generals, the Ghost Warriors retain the basic designs of their mortal clothes upon becoming ghosts, and since Soul Archer used to originate from Ninjago, then all warriors sharing the same clothes design pattern implies they used to live in Ninjago.

The third reason is similar to Skulkin being considered to be from Ninjago because of those were the only two known realms at that time. While the Sixteen other realms were established in Possesion, aside from the Cloud Kingdom, Ninjago was the only realm to contain humans until 2019, and sice then, each realm's human population have unique designs to make them distinct from one another. The sets for Possession also imply that the Ghost Warriors used to be regular farmers or civilians, with 70734 Master Wu Dragon showing cursed food stalls and ghosts' using rakes. No other realms have currently shown humans being farmers in the decade since.

(Consider Will you enter the Dream World? non-canon) by Samurai viper

(Consider Will you enter the Dream World? non-canon) by Samurai viper[]

When the shorts came out, it was initionally stated that the Will you enter the Dream World? shorts were deemed non-canon, but was later changed by Ninja72, who argued that their canon-status was unknown and could potentially be real. However, I believe that these shorts should indeed be categorized as non-canon due to their inconsistencies with the main storyline. For instance, if the shorts were canon, it would imply that the Dream World depicted in Dreamzzz is a real dimension within Ninjago and it influences the realms via sleep and they are not real dreams in the traditional sense, which appears to be the case for characters like P.I.X.A.L.. This notion is never acknowledged by the ninja characters, who, despite being able to recall their dreams, do not mention the Dream World or the Nightmare King, who Zane actually encountered in his dream. Even when asked if the Nightmare King could be a threat to the ninja, Tommy Andreasen simply answered that Ninjago exists merely as a television show within the context of Dreamzzz (https://x.com/TommyAndreasen/status/1691498050701676546) along with the fact that the shorts are simply just teasers for Dreamzzz (https://x.com/TommyAndreasen/status/1757723864853786666). And the fact that if the shorts were canon, it would mean that characters from Dreamzzz like Logan and Mrs. Castillo would have to exist as either real characters from some realm or dream manifestations, who has to be dreamt up by someone to exist, within the Ninjago franchise.

Decide on how Elements for dragons are listed by LB07productions

Decide on how Elements for dragons are listed by LB07productions[]

With recent information being revealed by Chris "Doc" Wyatt regarding elemental powers/essences used dragons and many editing conflicts occuring in the past weeks, I made this vote for editors to come to certain conclusions.

Discussion #1: Dragons using Creation. Last month, Doc Wyatt stated that dragons and oni are born with Creation and Destruction respectively.[11] Every known Oni and hybrids already had Destruction added as their essence beforehand, but currently, only Firstbourne and the Ultra Dragon have Creation in their page while all dragon-hybrids now have Creation as well. From the conclusion I came up with, it seems that only dragons who are known to be able to use all 4 elements can have the Creation essence, which I don't think is that correct for the following reasons:

  • Creation is not an element power and works differently, in simple forms, it is the powers used by dragons, it wouldn't be that big of a stretch that most dragons have the essence, but are limited to only use one of the 4 elements.
  • Destruction, Creation's natural opposite also has respective abilities specially embodied in the Oni Masks and later used by Garmadon like telekinesis, shapshifting/four arms and indestructiblity, but not all Oni have/use these abilities, yet they are users of Destruction.

So I have two suggestions, you can only support one but oppose both: add Creation to all dragons who use at least 1 of the Elements of Creation as they are born with that or take the fact that Creation is the power of the Dragons literally and have all dragons be users of Creation since it is possible that other abilities like pyrokinetic breath (but excluding Djinjagan Dragon's magic) are dragon abilities that could be tied to the raw essence.

All Dragons who use any of the Main Elements have Creation

Other discussions: Comments

All of these recent confirmations are retroactive and in some way feel contradictory. Prior to recently/Dragons Rising:

  • Creation the essence was never implied to have been explicitly used by dragons. All notions of dragons having the power to create were very metaphorical, and since Creation is comprised of different elements, it was more implied that the First Spinjitzu Master was the one to create the element.
  • The only known types of dragons for the longest time were only of the 4 elements of creation. Tommy stated that they wanted to diversify the dragon types more, but due to budgets and time, things stuck with those 4 archetypes.[16] Wind Dragons were the exception, but even then it was stated that their nature and existence made for lore complications, especially with Wojira. This statement of Firstbourne having the elements of her spawn did not account for any other element.
  • Energy was originally a very unique case of an element, with Tommy stating that he thought of it more as an essence, that it was exclusive to Lloyd, and it was intrinsically linked to the Green Ninja prophesy, not to mention it having similar properties to Creation. Now Doc is throwing this element as various dragons willy nilly all in the name of element nomenclature mystery, and tweets and Bluesky posts only hold so much weight. Either he is not putting much thought into this or he's trying to make too many drastic changes.

Overall though, having the elements of her spawn I believe is only applicable to the time when the episode aired, so unless Doc explicitly says she has this and that element, they should not be listed. But anyways, thank you for taking charge with this vote. Brandini N (talk) 04:22, 4 October 2025 (UTC)

I agree with you Brandini, even when Crystalized ended, Tommy tried to retcon Wind Dragons to be adolescent dragons so that dragons would only be limited to Creation. I don't really agree with the notion that the FSM created Creation, since aside from Wu's illusions, and the tornado of Creation, the show really only focused Creation with the 4 elements from the start. Even in DR, the Core Water Dragon was specifically excluded and aside from the Matriarch, all dragons used the 4 elements. Regarding Energy, my personal headcanon is that since Arc Dragons' horns are tied to Source Dragons, the Matriarch got her element from the Life SD, and that the Wind Dragon in S9 was a young Arc tied to the Flow Dragon, even Daidan's chest-thing is similar to the Focus Arc. It's really funny now how the SD's who's two elements were the most distant from dragons in Seabound now is the Source of the most elements. LB07productions (talk) 04:40, 4 October 2025 (UTC)f

Merge the Foggy desert and Wastelands pages by LB07productions

Merge the Foggy desert and Wastelands pages by LB07productions[]

The "Foggy desert" has remained in the past year one of the few relevant Dragons Rising locations not to receive its own official name, and with Dorama's puppet's story continuing in an oddly similar location in "The Missing," following its previous appearance in "To Mysterium," it seems clear that the story implies that it is the same desert region with the chances of the puppet being able to travel large distances, most likely through sea, to be very small. Even the terrain look the same, with the pattern of recurring giant rocks not being present in other locations (the Fist Land notably having rounder rock formations while the wastelands and "the foggy desert" having more spiky and rugged rocks).

Also worth pointing out that while coincidental, Zane, Cole and Bonzle were able to travel to Mysterium using Dorama's scans of the area, and the First Land is close to Mysterium as well.

However, there is a minor inconsistency: the "foggy desert" is currently located in the Wyldness, while the wastelands belong to the Sea of Sands as revealed in Crosstalk. However, I don't think the statement about the Wyldness should be taken into account for the following reasons: the writers of the show have no involvement in the magazines, usually, while the magazines do have information about future installments like Ras being from the Wyldness, where Cole and Jay were in S1 and the F5's powers, the information are always from the installment right after the one the issue is tied to, and in the three released installments following that issue (DRS2P2 and DRS3P1 and 2), there has been no mention of the desert being tied to the Wyldness, or of the desert itself, meaning that the info that Dorama fleed to the Wyldness was purely speculative from the magazine writers. So if the "foggy desert"'s page info is moved to the wastelands, the most current info from the show would override the magazine's info.

Support

  1. LB07productions (talk) 11:41, 7 October 2025 (UTC)
  2. I completely support that we should merge these pages. About magazine info, the Wastelands are already located on the border between the First Land and Ninjago, so we can just mention in the trivia section that it also likely borders the Wyldness. Legor4ik (talk) 18:37, 8 October 2025 (UTC)
  3. The Foggy Desert page kind of feels like an incomplete burger now. ElementalPilot 11:26, October 9 2026 (UTC)

Oppose

  1. Ecto lad778 (talk) 18:41, 7 October 2025 (UTC)

  3. Trainerkn 17:32, 8 October 2025 (UTC)
  4. The puppet maybe just traveled? We know it can still move, so it's possible that it just started walkin from the Wyldness and arrived to the Wastelands.Kelpy (talk)

Neutral

  1. Seems a bit too speculitory, plus the wiki does consider info from the magazines cannon and it hasnt been contradicted directly so best to hold off Ecto lad778 (talk) 18:41, 7 October 2025 (UTC)
  2. Regarding the puppet being able to walk from the Wyldness to the wastelands, in the entirety of Dragons Rising, the Wyldness hasn't been shown to directly border any realm (it has also been indirectly referred as its own island when Nya pointed to the three different islands the dragon cores are in "Gangs of the Sea"). And regarding info from magazines being considered canon, there are still many examples of magazines stating wrong information like the elemental alliance fighting Wojira, the Overlord always existing, Bleckt and Roby being provious tournament champions and Zur being an Oni; and most the information that is considered canon is later backup up/doubled down by the show, while Dorama's desert being in the Wyldness wasn't. (Reduce the number of images in elements and other powers in galleries) by Samurai viper

(Reduce the number of images in elements and other powers in galleries) by Samurai viper[]

Since Season 3 came out, there has been a certain issue going on. Almost daily, I notice a flood of images being added to all the power pages or other articles, which has become increasingly annoying. There was a vote regarding this matter, and some users, like Ninjagostuffiguessidk, have applied the decision to articles such as Levo. However, when it comes to elements, other powers, and all that, the same rules seem to be ignored, leading to an influx of spam images in the episode galleries. It's important to remember that this issue is actually addressed in the Manual of Style, and yet most of the images listed here defy it.

Spinjitzu[]

Poison[]

Nokt gets drained of this element.

Quake[]

TSD Quake 4.png
TSD Quake 6.png

Thunderfang[]

I'm pretty sure these images were only uploaded just because of the soul energy.

Thunderfang final trailer shot.png
Thunderfang final trailer shot 2.png
Thunderfang final trailer shot 3.png


Zarkt[]

All of these images? They were uploaded with the sole purpose of just for the Misfortune page.

Technology[]

Dragon Spinjitzu[]

Lightning[]

White, blue and yellow lightning in Ninjago: Dragons Rising
Nya using Lightning
Nokt using Lightning
Nokt gets drained of this element.

Smoke[]

At least 33 of these images were uploaded today, but many of them seem to be spam or lack a clear focus on the element itself. It's puzzling why images like this were added to the gallery, especially when they appear to be included just because of Cinder's hands. Wasn't it mentioned in the vote that the images should primarily relate to the article to be included?

Cinder down.png
Nokt receiving this element and several others from the Elemental Cup
Nokt gets drained of this element.

Instead of uploading multiple images of a single scene, like four pictures of Thunderfang roaring in Episode 60, it would be more efficient to simply upload a GIF of that moment, as I did with Episode 49. It feels like I might be the only one concerned about this issue and actively trying to address it. In a wiki that promotes fairness, it seems unjust to limit the number of images for a character that appears in just one episode while allowing element that has appeared in two shows like Fire and Smoke to have numerous images. Therefore, I propose that we reduce the number of images in the powers gallery and eliminate any spam images or anything similar. This will also imply for characters and episodes, since most of the images are effecting those two as will.

Also, it's worth considering, if you're not a fan of people critiquing the wiki for its handling of spoilers, making assumptions, or repeating the same content verbatim across articles, what does it say when others raise concerns about the excessive use of images?

Decide if the Golden Weapons had Golden Power by LB07productions

Decide if the Golden Weapons had Golden Power by LB07productions[]

For the past months, I have been analysing Ninjago media to see if the Golden Weapons really did possess the Golden Power, the original show never really properly focused on it as the concept of GP was introduced after the Golden Weapons were written off in the original seasons, and ever since, the way the essence is described has changed, now being derived from all the Source Dragons and apparently being a combination of all elements, similar to Lloyd's powers, but not being limited to Creation.[17][18] It is a no brainer that the weapons use Creation (Wu in "Blue Lightning": "The Four Golden Weapons of Spinjitzu. Each possessing the power of Creation". Ninjago World Guide in the Battle Box: "The Four Golden Weapons are the most powerful tools of creation known to man...If used together, these four weapons control the Power of Creation". And their corrupted variants being called the Weapons of Destruction). But do we consider them having Golden Power just because they are made of gold? The Dragon Armor, while being powerless, is made of gold as well but not tied to the essence, and Master Wu's dragon is also Creation but has gold as well. However, as counter evidence, the Overlord needed the Golden Weapons to become the Golden Master and use Golden Power, but technically, the only remainders of Golden Power Lloyd still had in "Codename: Arcturus" was the four elements he shared with the ninja, and we know that the two essences are closely linked.[19] Another factor is the fact that Golden Power is described to be able to Destroy and Create according to The Book of Elemental Powers. But the weapons themselves only create, and the Mega Weapon is specifically stated to only be able to create and not destroy. While the Golden Weapons played a big role in Crystalized, Golden Power itself was never mentioned in the season, the weapons also always being called simply as the "Weapons of Spinjitzu"; even the Overlord's plans were to corrupt Creation, and the Golden Ultra Dragon, while having the word "Golden" in its name, is implied to just being connected to Creation ("All we can hope now is to prevent the powers of creation from falling into the Overlord's hands." "I think it's us. I mean, our powers.")

The vote is to at only have the weapons, and their other forms only have Creation for now, before there would be actual statements that it also has Golden Powers instead of relying on vague assumptions. The two essences are a bit vague on their distinctions and connections, and I like to pass on the discussion to other people.

Updating the Manual of Style involving Elemental Powers by AnonymousAnomani

Updating the Manual of Style involving Elemental Powers by AnonymousAnomani[]

Would currently like to push for infobox template to have a split in Elemental Powers into categories that belong primarily with their respective Elemental Masters (like the main ninja's inherited elements) and those gained temporarily through external means. The Ninjago universe has introduced numerous Elements over many seasons, with varied origins (Source Dragons, Elemental Essences, etc.). A rigid single-list format in the infobox can be confusing for readers trying to understand a character's core abilities but a clear separation could help ensure consistency by clarifying which powers were intrinsic with them and which were plot-specific. (Establish proper realm naming conventions for infoboxes) by Brandini N

(Establish proper realm naming conventions for infoboxes) by Brandini N[]

Right now there's a bit of contention regarding what names should used for various realms on specific infoboxes, and it has come to my attention that as far as I am aware there is no definitive "rule" for how to go about this. This proposal aims to establish a proper convention, and I have three options we could choose:

  • 1. Name the realms based on recency. This option would keep the most recent name of a realm consistent across the board for all inhabitants, locations, and whatnot (I.e. Firstbourne: First Land; Crag-Nor: Land of Madness; Daidan: Land of Monsters).
  • 2. Name the realms based on chronological existence. This option will vary across articles, but the realm names listed will go in tandem with when the article subject was born/created relative to the Merge (I.e. Firstbourne: Realm of Oni and Dragons; Crag-Nor: Realm of Madness; Daidan: Realm of Monsters).
  • 3. Name the realms based on chronological introduction. This option will also vary when applicable. Realm names will be listed in tandem with when the article subject was introduced; Pre-DR introductions will keep old nomenclatures and DR-onwards introductions will use the most recent name. (I.e. Firstbourne: Realm of Oni and Dragons; Crag-Nor: Land of Madness; Daidan: Land of Monsters).

Galleries update by Igorek2137

Galleries update by Igorek2137[]

Hi everyone, greetings to all on the wiki.

Some time ago we voted on improving how character galleries would be divided. This change, proposed by Brandini back in August - and by the way, an outstanding one - came into effect. However, I have the impression that some things were not fully explained or specified, and that is why I am writing this vote. I simply want to discuss a few issues that serve as a kind of supplement to those earlier changes. Some of the things I mention here are already rules, but they are either not being followed or have been forgotten.

First, I would start with Design variants. Most main characters, such as Lloyd, have Design variants as their own separate section in the "General" gallery. However, this is not the case for supporting characters, where "Design variants" often fall under the "In Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu" tab. Examples include Dogshank or Krux, who both have these categories under the series tab. Of course, these characters appeared basically only in Masters of Spinjitzu and only there can their variants be seen (which technically makes this not a factual error in their case), but this will not apply to all characters. Moreover, it breaks consistency. Therefore, the first point of this proposal would be to make sure that all "Design variants" sections are their own separate tab, placed after "Promotional media" and before screenshots from the series ("In Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu" or "In Ninjago: Dragons Rising").

The mentioned "Promotional media" tab is the second part that requires clarification regarding what belongs in it. Currently, it is usually divided into three parts: the first, unnamed one, is a kind of mishmash - CGI renders, various posters, stickers, screenshots from games or mini-shorts. The second tab is "Drawings by Tommy Andreasen" (sometimes his drawings, for some reason, are placed in the first part), and the third is GIFs. I suggest keeping this layout but adding a new sub-tab. Above all, this mixture seems to make little sense - barely chronologically arranged graphics featuring a character. I propose that this tab should include ONLY: CGI renders, official or approved graphics, official posters promoting seasons or promotional campaigns, album artworks, or other graphic representations of a character used for promotion. A new sub-tab I propose is "Ninjago Magazine posters," which would collect all posters featuring a given character that appeared in magazines. This is because there are quite a lot of such posters (even though we do not yet have most of their copies on the wiki - but we will), and a place should be made for them. We could even go further and create subsections within "Promotional media" for almost everything" "CGI renders", "Official graphics", etc. However, my main proposal is to create "Ninjago Magazine posters" and to clean up the images in this gallery. Everything in this tab (in both cases) would be arranged chronologically. As for how to handle graphics that do not fit the definition I gave above:

  • Stickers would get their own separate section. This would mean, for now, simply moving stickers to a "Stickers" section, which would be placed directly under the "Cards" section. A mass effort to add and organize stickers is still planned, so there is no point in subdividing them within the category right now - just move them from "Promotional media" to "Stickers."
  • ALL promotional videos (such as Wu-Cru or Meet the Ninja) should be treated primarily as mini-movies (shorts), not as promotional media. This would result in moving these images to the "Miscellaneous" page for characters that have such pages, and adding them there in the upper sections.
  • I have no idea how to treat screenshots from promotional videos for LEGO sets. Let me know how you see this, but only after reading everything, because this is not the end.

The last issue is the rule according to which all installments should receive their own separate sections. What does this mean in practice? Currently, many galleries have a tab at the very bottom called "In other media", which is a mixture of everything. My proposal assumes removing this tab and splitting the individual images apart. Each game should get its own sub-tab in the "Video game appearances" section - without exceptions, even if it is only a single image. An example of a well-organized gallery is the one for Lloyd. A lot of images from the "Promotional media" tab, which I discussed earlier, would probably end up here as well. Similarly, "Quest for the Lost Powers" should always be reduced from a full section to a sub-section under "Literature appearances," placed between the series/mini-movies and "Video game appearances."

To summarize the changes using the Krux gallery as an example:

  • One sticker from "Promotional media" will be moved to a separate "Stickers" tab at the very bottom of the page.
  • A separate sub-tab for Tommy Andreasen's drawings will be created and added.
  • The Krux graphic from The LEGO Ninjago Movie Videogame will be moved to the "Video game appearances" tab and the sub-tab "The LEGO Ninjago Movie Videogame." The same applies to one screenshot from the Wu-Cru game.
  • "Design variants" will become its own separate section above "In Ninjago: Masters of Spinjitzu".
  • Additionally, "Ninjago: Reimagined" will become a full section (not a sub-section as it is now), due to the fact that these shorts are not treated by the wiki as part of Masters of Spinjitzu but as a separate creation (Lloyd has these shorts in the "Miscellaneous" tab instead of Masters of Spinjitzu one).

As you can see, much of this is simply about inconsistencies in editing and in the rules we have already established. However, I have added a few things of my own, and now I'm going to struggle for a few minutes figuring out how to properly add sections to a vote on what I've written here…

Introduce noarchive template and retire nolink template by Wikifan988

Introduce noarchive template and retire nolink template by Wikifan988[]

I just made a template called {{noarchive}} which can be used in cases like this of dead links with no archive to be found - you just include the link in the template and it adds "(link obsolete; archive unavailable)" to the end. This is because I found myself adding the {{nolink}} template to several pages that actually still had links, they were just dead links, so "unavailable" was technically inaccurate. I believe this new template is a better option for those cases as it preserves the original source while still acknowledging its obsolescence. The reason for using a template rather than just copying the text "(link obsolete; archive unavailable)" every time is to make it easier to keep track of all pages using this formatting, similar to the "Citations needed" category (there could even be a category invented for any page using this template, called something like "Pages citing dead links").

Now there are still several pages using the nolink template where this wouldn't apply because no link was ever cited on the page to begin with. Though it doesn't look as nice, I propose that along with the use of the noarchive template, we revert back to just using the {{cite}} template for all instances of unsourced information (except for pages using the new noarchive template). This is for a few reasons, mainly because it feels misleading to have a regular-looking cite ref that ends up just saying "link unavailable" (more misleading, to me at least, than a cite ref whose source is listed but is still obsolete), and because in some of those cases there may indeed still be a link or source available somewhere, it just hasn't been found so far.

To summarize: I propose the {{noarchive}} template is introduced to cite obsolete links when no archives are available, and the {{nolink}} template is retired and replaced with {{cite}} or {{noarchive}} templates depending on the context.

Support

  1. Wikifan988 (talk) 03:05, 21 December 2025 (UTC)
  2. Fishlover34 (talk) 03:29, 21 December 2025 (UTC)
  3. Igorek2137 (talk) 10:21, 21 December 2025 (UTC)
